B&M
THE MOGUL
A simple wheel arrangement
with a long history.
A Mogul is a steam locomotive with a 2-6-0
wheel arrangement: two leading wheels followed
by six coupled driving wheels.
The arrangement gave railroads a useful
combination of flexibility and adhesion.
For the Boston & Maine, Moguls became part
of the everyday machinery of New England
railroading.
BOSTON & MAINE
The B-15 class
A turn-of-the-century New England workhorse.
01
1903
Boston & Maine began receiving its B-15
Moguls during the first years of the
twentieth century.
02
Manchester
American Locomotive Company's Manchester,
New Hampshire works built Boston & Maine
locomotives including No. 1455.
03
New England
B&M Moguls worked across a railroad that
connected industrial cities, mill towns,
branch lines, and northern New England.
"Two leading wheels.
Six drivers.
One unmistakable New England machine."
MOGULWORKS.CO
BOSTON & MAINE
1455
ALCO — MANCHESTER, N.H.
PRESERVED HISTORY
No. 1455
Boston & Maine No. 1455 was built by the
American Locomotive Company at its Manchester,
New Hampshire works in 1907.
The locomotive represents a direct connection
between B&M's steam-era operations and the
industrial history of New Hampshire.
After its railroad career, 1455 passed through
preservation collections and ultimately became
part of the Danbury Railway Museum collection.
Visit the Danbury Railway Museum →
TIMELINE
A century of history.
1903
B&M's B-15 Mogul era begins.
1907
No. 1455 is constructed at
ALCO's Manchester works.
1910s
B&M Moguls continue working freight
and local assignments across the system.
Steam Era
Dieselization gradually replaces
steam locomotives across the railroad.
Today
Surviving locomotives preserve the
memory of New England's steam era.
ABOUT MOGULWORKS.CO
Railroad history,
rebuilt for today.
MogulWorks.co celebrates the locomotives,
railroads, workshops, engineers, and communities
that made New England railroading possible.
